name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Trent Kelly running with large cash advantage
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Kelly's incumbency and roughly two-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing him at 96% all point to a comfortable Republican hold with little evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or major outside spending on Johnson's behalf would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Mississippi's first district is a deeply Republican seat, and Trent Kelly is seeking another term as its incumbent representative. Kelly has raised about $1 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democratic challenger Cliff Johnson, who has raised roughly $550,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets give Kelly about a 96% chance of winning.

With a strong Republican lean, an entrenched incumbent, and a well-funded campaign, the district is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot but is not seen as a factor.
